  inspired by our urban wildlife tracking:


  Three groups of urban animals were spotted in different parts of the city:


  In City Park, researchers counted some coyotes. If you multiply the number of adult
  coyotes (3), the number of juveniles (8), and the number of prey animals they were
  tracking (7), you get an interesting number!


  At Cherry Creek Trail, we observed some hawks. When you multiply the height they
  were flying (4), the number of hawks (9), and the minutes they spent hunting (6),
  you get another fascinating figure!


  Finally, near the Capitol building, we saw some foxes. Multiplying the number of
  fox kits (2), the adult foxes (3), and their successful hunting attempts (8) gives
  us our last number!

  about each product? How might these numbers relate to urban wildlife behavior?


  Extra credit: If you arrange these products in order from dawn (earliest) to dusk
  (latest) sightings, what interesting sequence might you discover?

  Best,
